newsitem.title: DENMARK: Quiet Danish bonds seen possibly falling further.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Danish bonds seen possibly falling further.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped back on Monday in a becalmed market on top of last week's record highs with dealers seeing further declines ahead.

"There are no major market moving data until Wednesday's U.S. January CPI and the America's financial sector is partially closed today due to President's Day. The falls are natural after last week's gains and could well continue," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.12 point from the start at 112.50, yielding 6.15 percent in turnover of 1.1 billion crowns while its March future rose 0.17 point to 112.13 with 97 contracts traded.
Dealers saw the benchmark 2006 trading within 112.40-60 range all day. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.10 point to 90.10.
The crown traded at 3.8115 per mark at 1225 gmt, down from around 3.8110 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 64 basis points.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling a total of one billion crowns worth of assorted state bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
